title: Bun Bo Hue Noodle Soup
seoTitle: Bun Bo Hue Noodle Soup | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Spicy lemongrass beef and pork noodle soup for ten
subtitle: Spicy lemongrass beef and pork noodle soup for ten
description: Beef shank and pork hock simmer with lemongrass, chili, and shrimp paste into a fiery aromatic broth. Serve over round rice noodles with thin beef, blood cake if available, herbs, and lime.

steps.title: Start the broth
steps.instruction: Cover beef shank and pork hock with water. Add lemongrass, charred onion, and shrimp paste. Simmer 2.5–3 hours, skimming often.

steps.title: Season boldly
steps.instruction: Remove solids, strain broth if desired. Season with fish sauce and chili oil until broth is spicy, salty, and aromatic.

steps.title: Shred braised meat
steps.instruction: Pull tender meat from shank and hock, slice or shred, and hold warm.

steps.title: Prep noodles and herbs
steps.instruction: Cook rice noodles, rinse, and divide into bowls. Plate basil, mint, and limes at the line.

steps.title: Build bowls
steps.instruction: Top noodles with shredded braised meats and raw beef slices. Ladle boiling broth over to cook raw beef. Serve with herbs and lime.

proTips: Freeze beef eye round 30 minutes for easier thin slicing.
Annatto oil adds classic red color if you have it.
Warn the hall—this is spicier than most station soups.
tonightSpread: Bun bo hue with herb plate, lime, and extra chili oil.
Vietnamese pickles for acid between spicy spoonfuls.
leftovers: Broth improves next day—skim fat cap before reheating.
Shredded meats become banh mi filling with pickles and mayo.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Bun bo hue brings real heat and depth—crews who think pho is too mild will respect this bowl. It is soup with attitude, perfect for cold nights when the hall needs something that punches back.
mealPrepNotes: Broth takes time but mostly unattended. Skim diligently. Shrimp paste smells strong but transforms the broth—do not skip. Herbs should be washed and piled high before service.
